content.title: Craft-Play Role Conflict | Collateral Prop Collapse and Reconciliation
content.summary: Establish a clearly adult group's cooperative making baseline, then split them into temporary opposing play roles through replaceable costume or wearable signals. Keep one fragile shared object visible inside the confrontation geography, connect one overcommitted gesture directly to its accidental collapse, hold the collective reaction and close only after everyone drops character and repairs or regroups around the retained consequence.

quick_start.input_format: clearly adult collaborators jointly make one lightweight communal prop + replaceable costume or wearable-device signals split temporary opposing play roles + fragile shared object remains visible before contact + one overcommitted performance directly causes accidental collapse + collective pause + drop character and repair or regroup
quick_start.recommended_input: Three adult museum educators arrange a foam planetarium and delicate balsa antenna, split into comet-cape and wearable-observatory roles, accidentally snag and collapse the antenna during mock play, then exchange an embarrassed look and rebuild it together with the fallen pieces retained.
required_anchors: Show all collaborators jointly making or arranging one communal prop before roles split.
Assign opposing play roles through clear but replaceable costume or wearable-device signals.
Connect one overcommitted gesture directly to the object's collapse and hold the collective reaction.
End after everyone drops character and shares or repairs the altered space.
usage_steps: Replace the example subject, setting, and surface details with an original concept.
Keep every required anchor and Creative DNA invariant causally visible.
Choose the MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 prompt and fill only the declared variable slots.
Check duration, event order, camera continuity, sound, and anti-copy constraints before generation.
applicable_scope: Establish a clearly adult group's cooperative making baseline, then split them into temporary opposing play roles through replaceable costume or wearable signals. Keep one fragile shared object visible inside the confrontation geography, connect one overcommitted gesture directly to its accidental collapse, hold the collective reaction and close only after everyone drops character and repairs or regroups around the retained consequence.
Original 4–15 second concepts that can preserve every required anchor.
MiniMax H3 or Seedance 2.0 projects that need a reusable causal video structure.
not_suitable_for: Requests that copy the source identity, setting, props, dialogue, or shot order.
Concepts that cannot show all required anchors inside the target duration.
Long-form exposition or unrelated multi-location stories without a compact causal chain.

creative_dna.mechanism: Begin with an original group of clearly adult collaborators jointly making or arranging one lightweight communal prop. Assign playful opposing roles through replaceable costume or wearable-device signals, then keep one visibly fragile shared object inside the confrontation geography before contact occurs. Let one overcommitted performance gesture cause that object to collapse, hold a collective pause long enough to register the unintended result, and end only after everyone drops the roles and repairs, gathers around or calmly shares the altered space. The reusable mechanism is cooperative baseline, role split, visible collateral risk, accidental consequence and group reconciliation—not the source pandas, faces, costumes, cardboard box, pinwheel, bamboo or stick tower, backyard, exact choreography, camera placement, animation treatment, Dreamina branding, creator identity or timing.

invariants.rule: Show all collaborators jointly making or arranging one communal prop before roles split.
invariants.purpose: Creates a cooperative baseline that the later conflict can visibly disturb.
invariants.ablation_failure: Without shared ownership, the collapse reads as generic destruction rather than an unintended group consequence.

invariants.rule: Assign opposing play roles through clear but replaceable costume or wearable-device signals.
invariants.purpose: Makes the temporary conflict readable without requiring dialogue or identity copying.
invariants.ablation_failure: If roles are ambiguous, the confrontation has no legible social structure.

invariants.rule: Keep one fragile shared object visible between the groups before contact.
invariants.purpose: Preloads a measurable collateral risk inside the scene geography.
invariants.ablation_failure: A prop that appears only when it breaks feels like an inserted gag.

invariants.rule: Connect one overcommitted gesture directly to the object's collapse and hold the collective reaction.
invariants.purpose: Turns motion into an observable unintended consequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: A cutaway collapse or instant recovery weakens causality and emotional timing.

invariants.rule: End after everyone drops character and shares or repairs the altered space.
invariants.purpose: Converts conflict into a complete reconciliation arc while retaining the consequence.
invariants.ablation_failure: Ending on victory or resetting the prop loses the social payoff.

slots.name: lead_subject
slots.constraint: An original stable subject or pair with a readable role.

slots.name: setting
slots.constraint: A new setting with fixed spatial anchors and no source-specific surface.

slots.name: escalation_variable
slots.constraint: One causal variable that changes through visible stages.

slots.name: performance_rule
slots.constraint: A restrained acting or motion rule that keeps the mechanism legible.

slots.name: camera_grammar
slots.constraint: An information order that proves each state without copying source shot boundaries.

slots.name: payoff
slots.constraint: A clean final physical, informational or social consequence.

slots.name: sound_family
slots.constraint: An original hierarchy of diegetic cues; no unsupported source-audio claim.

anti_copy_exclusions: the source panda-like children, faces, bodies, fur, proportions, clothing, bandanas, goggles and poses
the source leaf-backed villain costume, stacked cardboard control box, colored buttons, pinwheel and exact role arrangement
the source backyard, fence, bushes, sunset layout, bamboo or stick tower and loose craft materials
the source confrontation choreography, tower collapse, sitting pose, shot scale, timing and polished animation treatment
the source creator identity, Dreamina and Seedance 2.5 claims, watermark, overlay and branding
